# @actual-app/api versions the release train must REFUSE.
#
# Why this file exists: without it a rollback is silently undone within 24 hours.
# Revert package.json to the previous version and CURRENT is old while LATEST is
# still the bad version upstream. That is a strict FORWARD move, the direction
# check is satisfied, and the train re-upgrades to the broken version the next
# night. The rollback lasts exactly one run.
#
# The failure signature is the real cost: "I fixed it, it worked, it came back on
# its own" is far more expensive to debug than a straightforward failure, because
# the obvious hypothesis is that the fix was wrong.
#
# FORMAT CONTRACT (pinned by tests/unit/train_preflight.test.js):
#   - one entry per line
#   - everything from the first '#' to end of line is a comment and is stripped
#   - the entry is the FIRST whitespace-delimited token of what remains
#   - blank lines are ignored
#   - matching is EXACT string equality on that token, never substring or regex
#
# Example (do not uncomment; this is documentation):
#   26.8.0  # broke stdio framing, see #NNN, 2026-08-04
#
# IMPORTANT: the train checks out `ref: main` and never reads develop, so ONLY
# the copy of this file on main has any effect. A denylist entry that has not
# reached main does not protect anything. See the rollback runbook in
# docs/guides/DEPLOYMENT.md.
#
# Deleting this file does NOT disable the control: a missing or unreadable
# denylist fails the run RED, because an absent safety control is a failure and
# not a no-op.
